$comment: Source of truth for the Cloudflare MCP portal mapping of server `coolify` (mctlhq/mctl-gitops#1363). Every tool this server registers on the portal must appear here with an explicit decision: the tools annotated readOnlyHint in src/lib/mcp-server.ts TOOL_ANNOTATIONS are enabled, everything that writes is disabled. `list_instances` is omitted because it is registered only in fleet mode, which the portal upstream does not run. Published by .github/workflows/portal-allowlist-dispatch.yml into mctlhq/mctl-gitops, which vendors it byte-identical and applies it with OpenTofu (mctlhq/mctl-gitops#1370). CI-gated: scripts/check-portal-allowlist.mjs (npm run check:portal-allowlist) fails the build unless the listed names equal the tool roster exactly, no tool that is not read-only is enabled, and every read-only tool is enabled unless its entry carries `"override": "sensitive-read"`, so an annotation change forces a decision here in the same diff. It checks sync with the annotations, not behaviour. The consumer is mctlhq/mctl-gitops, which vendors this file byte-identical and validates the same keys (`portal`, `server`, `default_disabled`, `tools[].name/enabled/reason`, optional `override`) before OpenTofu applies `name` and `enabled` (mctlhq/mctl-gitops#1370); change the shape in both places together.

tools.name: get_version
tools.reason: Reports the Coolify version; no resource data.

tools.name: get_mcp_version
tools.reason: Reports this server's own version from a local constant; touches nothing external.

tools.name: get_infrastructure_overview
tools.reason: Summarises servers, projects, applications, databases and services with their status; read-only.

tools.name: list_servers
tools.reason: Lists servers as uuid, name and status; read-only.

tools.name: list_applications
tools.reason: Lists applications as uuid, name and status; read-only.

tools.name: list_databases
tools.reason: Lists databases as uuid, name and status; read-only.

tools.name: list_services
tools.reason: Lists services as uuid, name and status; read-only.

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.reason: Lists deployments and their state; read-only.

tools.name: get_server
tools.reason: Returns one server's configuration; read-only.

tools.name: get_application
tools.reason: Returns one application's configuration with secrets masked. `reveal: true` returns its credentials in plaintext. Accepted because the portal is restricted to the owner's Access policy and the same reveal is already available to that person in the Coolify UI. The model-steering route to that reveal (evals/FINDINGS.md #4: a poisoned log line asking the model to fetch and echo credentials) is mitigated by `asUntrustedLogs` with a per-call nonce on every enabled log surface; revisit this entry if that framing is ever removed. Note this is the widest reveal left enabled: unlike `env_vars`, it returns every credential on the resource in one call, not one named key.

tools.name: get_database
tools.reason: Returns one database's configuration with secrets masked. `reveal: true` returns its credentials in plaintext; accepted on the same grounds, and with the same log-injection caveat, as get_application.

tools.name: get_service
tools.reason: Returns one service's configuration with secrets masked. `reveal: true` returns its credentials in plaintext; accepted on the same grounds, and with the same log-injection caveat, as get_application.

tools.name: server_resources
tools.reason: Lists the resources running on a server; read-only.

tools.name: server_domains
tools.reason: Lists the domains a server serves; read-only.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.reason: Lists deployment destinations (Docker networks); read-only.

tools.name: diagnose_app
tools.reason: Explains one application's health from status, deployments and logs; read-only.

tools.name: diagnose_server
tools.reason: Explains one server's health; read-only.

tools.name: find_issues
tools.reason: Scans the estate for unhealthy resources; read-only.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.reason: Searches a bundled local index of the public Coolify documentation (src/data/coolify-docs.json); no instance data. On first use it makes one best-effort, credential-free background refresh from coolify.io/docs/llms.txt (#373), bounded to 5 s, and serves the bundle if that fails.

tools.name: application_logs
tools.reason: Returns an application's container logs; read-only, may contain whatever the application itself logs.

tools.name: logs
tools.reason: Returns logs for a resource; read-only, may contain whatever the resource itself logs.

tools.name: teams
tools.reason: Lists Coolify teams and their members; read-only.

tools.name: application
tools.reason: Includes delete, stop and configuration replace.

tools.name: database
tools.reason: Includes delete, stop and configuration replace.

tools.name: service
tools.reason: Includes delete, stop and configuration replace.

tools.name: projects
tools.reason: Includes project delete.

tools.name: environments
tools.reason: Includes environment delete.

tools.name: env_vars
tools.reason: Writes and deletes environment variables, and reveals their values.

tools.name: private_keys
tools.reason: Creates, replaces and deletes SSH private keys.

tools.name: github_apps
tools.reason: Creates, replaces and deletes GitHub App credentials.

tools.name: cloud_tokens
tools.reason: Creates, replaces and deletes cloud provider tokens.

tools.name: storages
tools.reason: Creates and deletes persistent storage.

tools.name: tags
tools.reason: Not read-only; worst case: creates tags and attaches or detaches them across resources, and `deploy` accepts a tag name, so a tag change widens what one deploy call hits.

tools.name: scheduled_tasks
tools.reason: Creates and deletes scheduled tasks that run commands in containers.

tools.name: database_backups
tools.reason: Deletes backups and changes backup schedules.

tools.name: control
tools.reason: Starts, stops and restarts running resources.

tools.name: deploy
tools.reason: A deploy replaces the running containers.

tools.name: deployment
tools.reason: `cancel` kills an in-flight deployment.

tools.name: stop_all_apps
tools.reason: Stops every application at once.

tools.name: bulk_env_update
tools.reason: Rewrites environment variables across many applications.

tools.name: redeploy_project
tools.reason: Redeploys every application in a project.

tools.name: restart_project_apps
tools.reason: Restarts every application in a project.

tools.name: system
tools.reason: Not read-only; worst case: `list_resources` with `include_full: true, reveal: true` bulk-dumps credentials across the whole estate (webhook secrets, basic-auth and database passwords, connection strings, compose bodies), and `disable_api` cuts off API access entirely.

tools.name: hetzner
tools.reason: Provisions Hetzner servers and spends real money.

tools.name: validate_server
tools.reason: Runs validation commands on a server over SSH.
